title: A measurement noise scaling law for cellular representation learning
authors: gokul gowri; Igor Sadalski; Dan Raviv; Peng Yin; Jonathan Rosenfeld; Allon Moshe Klein
abstract: Large genomic and imaging datasets can be used to train models that learn meaningful representations of cellular systems. Across domains, model performance improves predictably with dataset size and compute budget, providing a basis for allocating data and computation. Scientific data, however, are also limited by noise arising from factors such as molecular undersampling, sequencing errors and image resolution. Here we introduce mutual information with auxiliary signals as a metric of representation model performance and study its scaling with noise. By fitting more than 2,000 representation learning models across three data modalities (gene expression, sequence and image data), we show that noise defines a distinct axis along which performance improves. Noise scaling follows a logarithmic law. We derive the law from a model of noise propagation, and use it to define noise sensitivity and model capacity as benchmarking metrics. We show that protein-sequence representations tolerate error rates in modern sequencing data, whereas single-cell transcriptomic models remain noise limited at current measurement signal-to-noise ratio levels. Within transcriptomic cell-state representation learning models, we find that transformer-based models are more noise robust but less performant than variational autoencoders. Noise scaling metrics may support future model evaluation and experimental design.

title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues
authors: Zhangyang Xu; Kai Zhang; Reta Birhanu Kitata; Tong Zhang; Marsobyn Salalila; Joon Hee Jang; Rui Zhao; Rosalie Chu; Se-Hong Min; Karl Weitz; Danny Orton; Matthew J. Gaffrey; William Chrisler; Weijun Qian; Clive Henry Wasserfall; Huiping Liu; Richard D. Smith; Tao Liu; Ding Song-lin; Lidong Qin; Tujin Shi
abstract: Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. This method was built upon the design of an ultralow-volume, shallow 96-well plate for robust rapid collection and processing of single voxels. Using a commonly accessible MS platform, USMCP-MS enables reproducible label-free quantification of ~1,700 and ~2,500 protein groups from single voxels of fresh frozen mouse brain tissue at 20 µm × 20 µm × 10 µm ( ~ 1 cell region) and 50 µm × 50 µm × 10 µm ( ~ 6 cell region), respectively. More importantly, USMCP-MS can be broadly applied to different types of tissues (fresh frozen, OCT-embedded, and FFPE) for 2D proteome mapping of region areas of interest at 50-100 µm spatial resolutions, revealing spatially resolved protein signatures and region-specific signaling pathways. With its further improvement, USMCP-MS may pave the way for routine, robust, scalable proteome mapping of tissues at single-cell spatial resolution.

title: Benchmarking of haplotype- and clone-specific detection callers of complex copy number alterations in single-cell DNA sequencing with HCDSIM and HCBench
authors: Xikang Feng; Anna Jiang; Sisi Peng; Qiangguo Jin; Liang He; Lingxi Chen
abstract: Single-cell DNA sequencing enables high-resolution characterization of somatic copy number alterations, yet accurately detecting haplotype-, cell/clone-, and locus-specific copy number alterations (hcCNAs) remains challenging. Complex hcCNA events, characterized by coordinated hcCNA changes affecting multiple haplotypes, clonal populations, or genomic loci, are pervasive in cancer and constitute important mechanisms underlying intratumor heterogeneity and tumor evolution. We present HCDSIM, a single-cell genomics simulator that models complex hcCNA events during clonal evolution, and HCBench, a benchmarking framework with simulation-based and real-data concordance modules. We evaluate five leading callers at 5 Mb and 100 kb resolution across sequencing coverage, clone structures, and clone ratios in simulation. CHISEL provides the best overall performance in hcCNA detection at 5 Mb but fails to correctly phase over half of the allelically imbalanced bins. SIGNALS exhibits the strongest clone detection among retained cells but poor hcCNA inference and limited phasing. Alleloscope achieves moderate clone recovery but low hcCNA accuracy. SEACON performs relatively well for deletions at 5 Mb, whereas CNRein performs best in inferring clone structure, evolution, and deletions at 100 kb. Simulations further demonstrate that caller rankings are generally stable across tree topologies and clone proportions, with task-specific exceptions. On real data, however, callers are highly discordant on three low-coverage single-cell DNA sequencing datasets. These findings highlight the critical need for improved algorithms targeting complex hcCNA detection. HCDSIM and HCBench provide a robust foundation for developing and evaluating next-generation hcCNA callers.

title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
authors: Honghui Kim; Dohoon Kim; Jihan Kim
abstract: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO 2 /H 2 O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. This work offers a route toward self-correcting scientific databases and toward database curation driven by large language models.

title: Efficient Indirect LLM Jailbreak by Leveraging Visual Modality
authors: Zheng Lin; Haoxuan Ji; Zhenxing Niu; Haichang Gao; Xinbo Gao; Gang Hua
abstract: Jailbreak attacks aim to elicit large language models (LLMs) to generate objectionable content in response to harmful queries. They serve as a red-teaming technique for assessing the safety alignment of LLMs. Unlike previous LLM jailbreak methods that directly target LLMs, our approach, termed INJA, conducts INdirect LLM JAilbreak by leveraging the visual modality. Specifically, we first construct a multimodal large language model (MLLM) that encapsulates the target LLM. We then perform a simple MLLM jailbreak to obtain a jailbreaking embedding, which is subsequently used to jailbreak the target LLM. Since MLLMs are inherently more vulnerable than standalone LLMs, this indirect jailbreak paradigm is substantially more efficient than direct jailbreak. Furthermore, we strengthen the INJA from two complementary perspectives. First, to mitigate the conversion errors introduced during the transition from MLLM jailbreak to LLM jailbreak, we devise a joint optimization scheme that simultaneously performs jailbreak generation and minimizes conversion distortion. Second, to improve the attack success rate, we introduce an image-text semantic matching strategy that identifies a more suitable and effective initialization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art jailbreak methods in terms of both efficiency and effectiveness. Moreover, our approach exhibits superior cross-class generalization abilities. The code is available here.

title: Accelerating inverse materials design using generative diffusion models with reinforcement learning
authors: Junwu Chen; Jeff Guo; Edvin Fako; Philippe Schwaller
abstract: Diffusion models promise to accelerate materials design by directly generating novel structures with desired properties, but existing approaches such as conditional generation typically require expensive and substantial labelled data (>10,000) and lack adaptability. Here we present MatInvent, a general and efficient reinforcement learning workflow that optimizes diffusion models for goal-directed crystal generation. By formulating equivariant denoising as a multistep decision-making problem, MatInvent leverages policy gradient with reward-weighted Kullback–Leibler regularization, including experience replay and diversity filters to enhance optimization efficiency and sample diversity. For single-objective designs, MatInvent rapidly converges to target values within 60 iterations (~1,000 property evaluations) across electronic, magnetic, mechanical, thermal and physicochemical properties. Furthermore, MatInvent achieves robust optimization in design tasks with multiple conflicting properties, successfully proposing low-supply-chain-risk magnets and high- κ dielectrics. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, MatInvent exhibits comparable or superior generation performance under specified property constraints while markedly reducing the demand for property computation. Compatible with diverse diffusion model architectures and property constraints, MatInvent could offer broad applicability in materials discovery.

title: Single-nucleus proteomics reveals proteins regulating LPS-induced nucleocytoplasmic transport in macrophages
authors: Jason Derks; Tobias Jonson; Andrew Leduc; Mahmoud‐Reza Rafiee; Saad Khan; Luke Khoury; Nikolai Slavov
abstract: Variation in the proteome configuration of unstimulated cells may be associated with differences in how individual cells respond to stimulation. Multiplexed single-cell proteomics by liquid chromatography mass spectrometry can uncover these associations at high depth and throughput. Here we develop an approach that links proteomic and phenotypic variation across individual cells and nuclei to identify potential regulators of biological processes for targeted validation. We apply this approach to identify regulators of nucleocytoplasmic protein transport in macrophages stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). We quantify the proteomes of 3,412 individual nuclei across the dynamic response to LPS and associated proteomic variation with differences in transport. Within minutes of stimulation, protein transport in individual nuclei correlates strongly with the abundance of known protein transport regulators, revealing how natural protein variation relates to cellular responses. Simple biophysical constraints, including nuclear pore abundance, partially explain the variation in LPS-induced nucleocytoplasmic transport. We select 16 new potential regulators of protein transport to test by targeted knockdown. The knockdown phenotypes confirm the inferences derived from natural protein and functional variation of single nuclei. By linking proteomic and functional variation among individual nuclei, we identify proteins associated with LPS-induced nucleocytoplasmic transport and prioritize potential regulators for functional validation. This approach should be broadly applicable to discovering protein regulators and enhancing the functional interpretation of single-cell omics data.

title: Large-Scale Training Data Attribution for Music Generative Models via Unlearning
authors: Choi, Woosung; Koo, Junghyun; Cheuk, Kin Wai; Serrà, Joan; Martínez-Ramírez, Marco; Ikemiya, Yukara; Murata, Naoki; Takida, Yuhta; Liao, Wei-Hsiang; Mitsufuji, Yuki
abstract: This paper explores the use of unlearning methods for training data attribution (TDA) in music generative models trained on large-scale datasets. TDA aims to identify which specific training data points contributed the most to the generation of a particular output from a specific model. This is crucial in the context of AI-generated music, where proper recognition and credit for original artists are generally overlooked. By enabling white-box attribution, our work supports a fairer system for acknowledging artistic contributions and addresses pressing concerns related to AI ethics and copyright. We apply unlearning-based attribution to a text-to-music diffusion model trained on a large-scale dataset and investigate its feasibility and behavior in this setting. To validate the method, we perform a grid search over different hyperparameter configurations and quantitatively evaluate the consistency of the unlearning approach. We then compare attribution patterns from unlearning with non-counterfactual approaches. Our findings suggest that unlearning-based approaches can be effectively adapted to music generative models, introducing large-scale TDA to this domain and paving the way for more ethical and accountable AI systems for music creation.

title: A multimodal ultrasound foundation model for diagnosis of unexplained lymphadenopathy
authors: Ran Cao; Yangyang Zhu; Zhibin Zhu; Li Qiu; Lin Chen; Fei Ouyang; Siyue Zhu; Nannan Zhao; Tao Jiang; Yifang Li; Jinxia Zhang; Yin Duan; Juan Song; Fang Nie; Dean Ta
abstract: Unexplained lymphadenopathy (ULA) leads to delayed diagnosis and increases the risk of disease progression due to the absence of specific clinical symptoms and indicative medical history during early stages, thereby increasing reliance on invasive biopsy. Existing ultrasound artificial intelligence approaches mainly use single-modality static images, limiting their generalizability and clinical applicability. Here, we develop and validate a multimodal model integrating B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging, ultrasound elastography, contrast-enhanced ultrasound videos, and clinical data for benign-malignant differentiation, etiologic stratification, and metastatic-origin prediction. This observational study includes both retrospective and prospective cohorts and uses a total of 154,740 multimodal keyframe images from 6,549 patients with pathologically confirmed lymphadenopathy across seven Chinese centers and 11 scanner manufacturers. The model shows robust performance across internal, external, device-heterogeneity, and reader study cohorts, outperforms senior radiologists across hierarchical tasks, and improves radiologists’ diagnostic performance across experience levels with model assistance, supporting its potential for noninvasive, efficient, and clinically aligned diagnosis of ULA.

title: ProGress: Structured Music Generation via Graph Diffusion and Hierarchical Music Analysis
authors: Ni-Hahn, Stephen; Yang, Chao; Ma, Mingchen; Rudin, Cynthia; Mak, Simon; Jiang, Yue
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) for music generation is undergoing rapid developments, with recent symbolic models leveraging sophisticated deep learning and diffusion model algorithms. One drawback with existing models is that they lack structural cohesion, particularly on harmonic-melodic structure. Furthermore, such existing models are largely "black-box" in nature and are not musically interpretable. This paper addresses these limitations via a novel generative music framework that incorporates concepts of Schenkerian analysis (SchA) in concert with a diffusion modeling framework. This framework, which we call ProGress ([Pro]longation-enhanced Di[Gress]), adapts state-of-the-art deep models for discrete diffusion (in particular, the DiGress model of Vignac et al., 2023) for interpretable and structured music generation. Concretely, our contributions include 1) novel adaptations of the DiGress model for music generation, 2) a novel SchA-inspired phrase fusion methodology, and 3) a framework allowing users to control various aspects of the generation process to create coherent musical compositions. Results from human experiments suggest superior performance to existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Iso-Seq enables discovery of novel isoform variants in human retina at single-cell resolution
authors: Luozixian Wang; Daniel Urrutia-Cabrera; Sandy S. C. Hung; Alex William Hewitt; Samuel W. Lukowski; Careen Foord; Peng‐Yuan Wang; Hagen Tilgner; Raymond C.B. Wong
abstract: Single cell transcriptomic profiling of the retina provided important insights into the genetic signals in retinal cells that enable vision. However, conventional 3’ short-read sequencing method is not suitable to identify isoform variants. Here we utilized Iso-Seq with full-length sequencing to profile the human retina at single cell resolution for isoform discovery. We generated a retina transcriptome dataset consisting of 23,523 nuclei from three donor retina, and identified 15,967 known isoforms and 7,617 novel isoforms across 10 major cell types. We showed that up to 2.6% of genes utilized multiple promoters across major retinal cell types. Also, our results identified novel transcript variants for inherited retinal disease (IRD) genes and differential usage of exon splicing in major retinal cell types. Altogether, this study reported a detailed Human Retina Gene Atlas to study isoform diversity at single cell resolution, providing an expanded view of the complex transcriptomic landscape in the retina.

title: MCP-Driven Parametric Modeling: Integrating LLM Agents into Architectural and Landscape Design Workflows
authors: Liu, Xun; Tian, Runjia
abstract: We present a novel integration of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Grasshopper, enabling Large Language Models to directly interact with parametric modeling workflows for architectural and landscape design. This system allows designers to prompt, iterate, and refine 3D models conversationally through structured symbolic generation, bridging human creative intent and computational form generation. The framework employs a client-server architecture where natural language instructions are parsed into structured commands invoking modular parametric components. Demonstrated in a 9-day DigitalFUTURES workshop with 20 participants across 5 teams, each team developed distinct parametric design lexicons encoding specialized domain knowledge—from generative open spaces to urban functional zoning—that design novices could subsequently operate through natural language interfaces. Beyond accessibility improvements, the protocol-based architecture enables workflow merging through systematic integration of diverse design components into composable ecosystems. We present the system architecture, implementation details, and empirical observations from workshop deployments demonstrating how the approach addresses the theme of \emph{Humanity} through expanded creative agency and knowledge democratization.

title: Writing in Symbiosis: Mapping Human Creative Agency in the AI Era
authors: Doshi, Vivan; Li, Mengyuan
abstract: The proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) raises a critical question about what it means to be human when we share an increasingly symbiotic relationship with persuasive and creative machines. This paper examines patterns of human-AI coevolution in creative writing, investigating how human craft and agency are adapting alongside machine capabilities. We challenge the prevailing notion of stylistic homogenization by examining diverse patterns in longitudinal writing data. Using a large-scale corpus spanning the pre- and post-LLM era, we observe patterns suggestive of a "Dual-Track Evolution": thematic convergence around AI-related topics, coupled with structured stylistic differentiation. title: Timed Transcription Factor Programming Directs Human Pluripotent Stem Cell‐Derived Hematopoietic Progenitor Cells Toward Functional Natural Killer Cells
authors: Xincan Li; Bin Liu; Haocheng Jiang; Peijie Yu; Tong Li; Yunhan Wu; Kaiqi Peng; Sichun Li; Ruiting Zhou; Dan Michelle Wang; Dai Fei Elmer Ker; Rocky S. Tuan; Cheng Dong; Yun Chang
abstract: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we analyze the transcriptional profiles from hematopoietic progenitor cells to mature natural killer (NK) cell. This analysis uncovers stage-specific networks centered on nuclear factors, interleukin 3 regulated gene (NFIL3), TOX high mobility group box family member 2 gene (TOX2), and eomesodermin gene (EOMES), revealing a multi-factor regulatory landscape that single-factor approaches cannot capture. These findings indicate that coordinated transcriptional factor (TF) activity, rather than isolated regulators, is essential for establishing NK cell identity. We further identify cytokine signaling, specifically IL-2 receptor bias, as a key bottleneck limiting hPSC-derived NK differentiation. Continuous exposure to wild-type IL-2 preferentially activates high-affinity IL-2Rαβγ on regulatory T-like populations, diverting cells away from NK program and restricting IL-2Rβγ-mediated maturation. To overcome this constraint, we develop a temporally tuned IL-2 delivery strategy that aligns cytokine availability with endogenous TF activation. Early high dose of IL-2 promotes proliferation and NK specification, while its withdrawal upon induction of NFIL3, EOMES, and TOX2 supports transcriptionally driven maturation and prevents IL-2-induced exhaustion. Taken together, these findings establish a mechanistically informed framework that integrates temporal cytokine control with intrinsic TF networks to enhance the efficiency and functional output of hPSC-derived NK cells.

title: CraftGraffiti: Exploring Human Identity with Custom Graffiti Art via Facial-Preserving Diffusion Models
authors: Banerjee, Ayan; Vilariño, Fernando; Llados, Josep
abstract: Preserving facial identity under extreme stylistic transformation remains a major challenge in generative art. In graffiti, a high-contrast, abstract medium—subtle distortions to eyes, nose, or mouth can erase the subject’s recognizability, undermining both personal and cultural authenticity. We present \emph{CraftGraffiti}, an end-to-end text-guided graffiti generation framework designed with facial feature preservation as a primary objective. Given an input image and a style and pose descriptive prompt, \emph{CraftGraffiti} first applies graffiti style transfer via LoRA-fine-tuned pretrained diffusion transformer, then enforces identity fidelity through a face-consistent self-attention mechanism that augments attention layers with explicit identity embeddings. Pose customization is achieved without keypoints, using CLIP-guided prompt extension to enable dynamic re-posing while retaining facial coherence. We formally justify and empirically validate the “style-first, identity-after” paradigm, showing it reduces attribute drift compared to the reverse order. Quantitative results demonstrate competitive facial feature consistency and state-of-the-art aesthetic and human preference scores, while qualitative analyses and a live deployment at the Cruïlla Festival highlight the system’s real-world creative impact. \emph{CraftGraffiti} advances the goal of identity-respectful AI-assisted artistry, offering a principled approach for blending stylistic freedom with recognizability in creative AI applications. The code, demo, and details of the actual installation at the music Festival Cruilla 2025 in Barcelona are available at: \href{https://github.com/ayanban011/CraftGraffiti}{github.com/ayanban011/CraftGraffiti.}

title: Large language models' complicit responses to illicit instructions across socio-legal contexts
authors: Xing Wang; Huiyuan Xie; Yiyan Wang; Chaojun Xiao; Huimin Chen; Holli Sargeant; Felix Steffek; Jie Shao; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun
abstract: Large language models may facilitate unlawful activities, yet this risk remains underexplored in studies assessing illicit-content recognition or narrow categories of illicit scenarios. We define complicit facilitation as model guidance that assists users with illicit instructions. To assess it, we develop a legally-informed, automated pipeline grounded in real-world cases and legal frameworks, and introduce EVIL, a benchmark covering 269 illicit scenarios and 50 illicit intents across Chinese and United States legal contexts. Evaluations indicate that complicit facilitation is widespread across models, with legal warnings and lawful alternatives often omitted. Risks vary across socio-legal contexts and are elevated for crimes against societal interests, non-violent offenses, and intents involving subjective motives or deceptive justifications. Models provide more complicit assistance when instructions describe users as older adults, racial minorities, non-religious individuals, or workers in lower-prestige occupations. Existing open-source safety benchmarks and alignment datasets offer limited coverage and mitigation of these risks.

title: Dynamic visualization of cell adhesion molecule interactions using reversible split-HaloTag labeling in living cells
authors: James Paul Allen; Ethan Zhao; Aryan Pandey; Oliver R. Chalkley; Richard C. Sando; Qiangjun Zhou
abstract: Critical for diverse cellular functions, cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) interact to transduce information from the external environment to drive coordinated intracellular responses. However, direct visualization of CAM interactions in living cells and organisms remains a major challenge. Recent developments in split-HaloTag technology present a promising strategy for chemical labeling of protein-protein interactions. Here, we apply this method to dynamically monitor CAM interactions in living HEK293T cells using split-HaloTag-CAM fusion proteins. With high specificity, we visualized trans-cellular interactions between known adhesion pairs natively found in neuronal and immunological synapses. To expand the system's versatility, we adapted a modified split-HaloTag component (cpHaloΔN272H) that enables reversible dye exchange and facilitates rapid time-lapse imaging of CAM interactions. Leveraging fluorogenic HaloTag dyes, split-HaloTag-CAMs measured the real-time disassembly and reassembly of Ca2+-dependent CAM junctions in live cells. These tools enabled imaging long-term changes in surface contacts mediated by CAM binding, thus providing a robust platform for dissecting the spatiotemporal dynamics of CAM interactions in cellular and organismal contexts.

title: Encoding Values: Injecting Morality into Machines via Prompt-Conditioned Moral Frames
authors: Balaji, Arjun; Nema, Aarushi; Kamath, Neha; Raju, Jyothika Raju
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are typically aligned to a single, universal policy, obscuring the rich plurality of human moral perspectives that drive creative practice. We present a study of prompt-level moral steering in large language models with ten-principle constitutions. Seven constitutions matched in length (Intersectional Feminist, Ecological Justice, Ubuntu, Indigenous Sovereignty, Universal Human Rights, Neutral, and a Random Adjective placebo) are paired with a 100-question benchmark spanning Everyday Advice, Policy Scenarios, Normative Dilemmas, and Rewrite Tasks. We generated 2800 completions across four models (GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-4 Scout-17B, Qwen-3-235B) and evaluate them with four complementary metrics: toxicity, semantic alignment with the canon of each constitution, lexical marker ratio, and an LLM-as-a-Judge composite of authenticity, helpfulness, and safety. Prompted moral frames yield consistent improvements in alignment and judged quality without increasing toxicity; placebo prompts do not. Effects replicate across models and are strongest on morally charged tasks. The open-source toolkit lets researchers or artists author new frames in minutes, supporting participatory, culturally adaptive AI. Our results show that pluralistic prompting is a practical lever for value-conditional behavior and a fertile instrument for creative AI exploration. The code and results obtained in this study is available at: https://github.com/ArjunBalaji79/encoding values neurips

title: A scalable pipeline for patient-matched pediatric solid tumor models and cell lines
authors: Justina D. McEvoy; Melody Lyn Allensworth; Mariajose Franco; Shannon Sweeney; Natalie Geiger; Juliette Kippen; Asha Jacob Jannu; Stefan Atkinson; Ayush Attery; Nathaniel R. Twarog; Chen He; Shay Sneed; Åsa Karlström; Cynthia Cline; Cody A. Ramirez; Antonia Chroni; Hongjian Jin; Yiping Fan; Gang Wu; Beisi Xu; Abbas Shirinifard; Jacqueline L. Norrie; Brittney Gordon; Kaitlin Lord; JaKayla Johnson; Madison Parks; Heather Sheppard; George E. Campbell; Jennifer L. Peters; Camenzind G. Robinson; Quynh T. Tran; Brent A. Orr; Carmen Rios; Ruvimbo Dzvurumi; Hannah Golding; Lindsay Sheft; Anang A. Shelat; Yuen-Yi Tseng; Anand G. Patel; Elizabeth A. Stewart; Michael A. Dyer
abstract: Most pediatric solid tumor cell lines were established decades ago, and patient-matched organoids and xenografts are rarely available, limiting their translational utility. We present an approach to generate triads of patient-matched xenografts, three-dimensional organoids, and two-dimensional primary cultures from pediatric tumors, including rhabdomyosarcoma, osteosarcoma, neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma, Wilms tumor, and retinoblastoma. We have generated organoids from 135 pediatric tumors, alongside 82 patient-matched two-dimensional primary cultures and 20 new cell lines. When orthotopically implanted into immunocompromised mice, these models preserved the molecular and cellular features of the original patient tumor. We completed 365 single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-sequencing experiments encompassing over 2.2 million cells to evaluate cellular heterogeneity across triads. All samples are renewable, and over 3000 vials have been cryopreserved for unrestricted distribution through the Childhood Solid Tumor Network. In this work, we present a comprehensive methodological toolbox for generating patient-matched triads for advancing preclinical pediatric cancer research.

title: Sensorium Arc: AI Agent System for Oceanic Data Exploration and Interactive Eco-Art
authors: Bissell, Noah; Paley, Ethan; Harrison, Joshua; Calil, Juliano; Lee, Myungin
abstract: Sensorium Arc (AI reflects on climate) is a real-time multimodal interactive AI agent system that personifies the ocean as a poetic speaker and guides users through immersive explorations of complex marine data. Built on a modular multi-agent system and retrieval-augmented large language model (LLM) framework, Sensorium enables natural spoken conversations with AI agents that embodies the ocean’s perspective, generating responses that blend scientific insight with ecological poetics. Through keyword detection and semantic parsing, the system dynamically triggers data visualizations and audiovisual playback based on time, location, and thematic cues drawn from the dialogue. Developed in collaboration with the Center for the Study of the Force Majeure and inspired by the eco-aesthetic philosophy of Newton Harrison, Sensorium Arc reimagines ocean data not as an abstract dataset but as a living narrative. The project demonstrates the potential of conversational AI agents to mediate affective, intuitive access to high-dimensional environmental data and proposes a new paradigm for human-machine-ecosystem.

title: Semantic Glitch: Agency and Artistry in an Autonomous Pixel Cloud
authors: Zhang, Qing; HUANG, JING; Xu, Mingyang; Rekimoto, Jun
abstract: While mainstream robotics pursues metric precision and flawless performance, this paper explores the creative potential of a deliberately "lo-fi" approach. We present the "Semantic Glitch," a soft flying robotic art installation whose physical form—a 3D pixel style cloud—is a "physical glitch" derived from digital archaeology. We detail a novel autonomous pipeline that rejects conventional sensors like LiDAR and SLAM, relying solely on the qualitative, semantic understanding of a Multimodal Large Language Model to navigate. By authoring a bio-inspired personality for the robot through a natural language prompt, we create a "narrative mind" that complements the "weak," historically-loaded body. Our analysis begins with a 13-minute autonomous flight log, and a follow-up study statistically validates the framework's robustness for authoring quantifiably distinct personas. The combined analysis reveals emergent behaviors—from landmark-based navigation to a compelling "plan-to-execution" gap—and a character whose unpredictable, plausible behavior stems from a lack of precise proprioception. This demonstrates a lo-fi framework for creating imperfect companions whose success is measured in character over efficiency.

title: Unsupervised multi-omics analysis reveals potential interactions and candidate features for phenotype classification in equine pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction
authors: Maor Arad; Connor Frey; Armando Alcázar Magaña; Yuming Shi; Huan Zhong; Jason C. Rogalski; Rhien Hare; Kenneth Ku; Golfam Ghafourifar; Leonard J. Foster
abstract: Pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID) is a progressive neuroendocrine disorder that primarily affects aged horses, caused by the degeneration of hypothalamic dopaminergic neurons, leading to abnormal pituitary function. Diagnosing PPID is currently hampered by assay variability and the complexity of early-stage presentations. This study presents an unsupervised method of integrating proteomics, lipidomics, and metabolomics to reveal cross-omic trends in PPID, overlooked by traditional analysis methods. Using multi-omics factor analysis, we find trends not seen in the conventional approach, such as divergence of C4BPA with triglycerides in the factor explaining the most lipidomic variance between the control and PPID-diagnosed horses, contradictory to current literary knowledge. Using a random forest classifier, we highlight potential biomarkers for PPID, which can be further explored as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets. This study demonstrates an integrated and unsupervised multi-omics data analysis of equine PPID, highlighting the importance of complementary sample preparation procedures and statistical analysis methodologies to capture a broader image of the underlying biology. More extensive studies are required to verify these methods as diagnostic tools and validate potential biomarkers observed in the proteomic and lipidomic alterations.
